entries.provider: native SOP verbs and normalized geometry buffers

entries.reverse_profile_coverage: The SHA-pinned libSOP extended profile resolves CookVerb and buildFromOp exports for Group Promote, Range, Expand, and Find Path and exports the real internal Cook bodies for all four nodes. Find Path additionally captures its 287-line control-pair builder and Edge, Point, Primitive, and Vertex domain apply functions at RVAs 0x4b91a70, 0x4b95d40, 0x4b96920, 0x4b97140, and 0x4b979c0 (579, 354, 414, and 488 domain-apply lines). A separate SHA-pinned libGU group-path-gu profile resolves and exports 14/14 GU_LoopHelper and GU_PathFinder functions plus 12 internal functions: the shared successor dispatcher, four successor constructors, UV edge compatibility, signed lnext/lprev, both real cost callbacks, and both heap-sift comparators. The recovered Range, Expand, and Find Path outer bodies are 1133, 1424, and 827 decompiled lines respectively, so singleton-return entry shells cannot be mistaken for implementation coverage.

entries.performance_contract_revision: v4 full output Geometry Cook with deterministic explicit edge buffers, four-domain input counts, exact prebound parameters, exact cold-versus-hot and repeated-hot post-Cook group contracts, checksum/normalization outside the timed Cook interval, and a 1 ms background sampler over current process Working Set throughout cold/warm/measured Cooks; the process-lifetime peak is retained only for audit because subtracting lifecycle high-water marks can falsely report zero after a larger startup peak
entries.performance_memory_validation: provider validators require one sampler thread, a 1 ms interval, sampled_peak_delta_bytes = sampled_peak_working_set_bytes - baseline_working_set_bytes, and process_lifetime_peak_working_set_bytes >= sampled_peak_working_set_bytes; negative tests cover every invariant. The sampler thread is running before baseline capture, so its own stable overhead is included on both providers rather than charged to either Cook.
entries.provider_self_check_2026_08_10: licensed Houdini matrix construction produced exactly 77 semantic and 15 performance unique IDs; five added square-grid cases pin short, segmented, long, and reverse equal-cost path arbitration
entries.probe_source_redline: houdini_group_native_probe.rs delegates deterministic normalization and post-65 semantic extensions to dedicated modules; the resulting files remain below the 1200-line redline and preserve one canonical execution/normalization path
entries.promote_hot_path_optimization: lazy half-edge topology acquisition plus allocation-free primitive-edge, vertex-edge, and edge-primitive scans; simple domain projections are guarded to leave the topology cache cold
entries.promote_edge_to_point_order_evidence: The complete libSOP promote_rule_apply@rva:0x4ba01b0 Edge-to-Point branch temporarily calls GA_ElementGroup::makeOrdered while inserting deduplicated endpoints, then explicitly calls setOrdered(false). Houdini SDK GA_ATIGroupBool.h confirms that false converts the group back to unordered, so group_core emits exact unordered final membership rather than preserving the temporary insertion sequence.
entries.range_ordered_base_evidence: libSOP range_verb_cook@rva:0x4ba8710 checks the detached base group's ordered storage and calls GA_ElementGroup::setOrdered on the destination before applying the range. group_core now evaluates windows, N-of-M positions, and connected-region numbering in the named ordered base sequence, emits the selected subsequence, and converts an existing merge destination to ordered before applying the rule; semantic cases range/ordered_base and range/ordered_merge_destination distinguish sequence behavior from sorted membership and cover sequential multiparm merge.
entries.range_hot_path_optimization: multiparm Range now borrows the shared per-domain adjacency and upgrades to an owned copy only when connectivity attributes or an active collision boundary mutate it; plain connected-component rules no longer clone the complete adjacency per rule. Range window and N-of-M selection also stream directly over members without allocating a temporary ranged vector.
entries.adjacency_hot_path_optimization: primitive and edge-ring adjacency builders reuse point and edge scratch vectors across primitives, eliminating per-primitive temporary allocations while preserving primitive iteration, edge insertion, final sorting, and deduplication order.
entries.find_path_edge_order_evidence: libSOP find_path_verb_cook@rva:0x4b8f200 explicitly calls GA_ElementGroup::makeOrdered for point, primitive, and vertex outputs, while its edge branch writes a GA_EdgeGroup without makeOrdered. group_core now retains path order for element groups but emits Houdini-compatible unordered edge-group storage; the edge-style semantic cases still validate exact edge membership and buffers.
entries.find_path_hot_path_optimization: Extend-to-edge no longer inserts each discovered front element at Vec index zero or materializes a candidate Vec per step. It tracks the frontier in forward state, records a compact prefix once, and uses the shared bit-mask substrate for membership, removing the long-path O(n^2) shift pattern without changing direction thresholds or deterministic tie-breaking.
entries.find_path_pair_builder_evidence: libSOP find_path_pair_builder@rva:0x4b91a70 proves Sequential Close appends exactly the last-to-first pair, while Pairs mode always consumes non-overlapping endpoint pairs and ignores Close for pair construction. group_core no longer schedules a redundant reverse Cook for every Pairs+Close pair; semantic case path/mode/pairs_close pins the parameter combination.
entries.find_path_cost_evidence: Houdini 22 toolkit GU_PathFinder.h exposes the exact inline successor masks and cost templates: BOUNDARY costs 0, QUAD_LEFT/QUAD_RIGHT costs 1, QUAD_OPPOSITE/OPPOSITE costs 99, fallback costs 100, and destination-half-edge Euclidean length is accumulated as the secondary key. libGU std::function vtables at VA 0x1868d4ea8 and 0x1868d5030 independently identify the matching real Edge Loop and Edge Ring relaxation callbacks at RVAs 0x5aada30 and 0x5aada40. Both callbacks also reject domain-specific collision and previous-path states. RVAs 0x5aae910 and 0x5aaeaa0 are separately named heap-sift functions and confirm the same integer-first/double-second ordering. The prior generic geometric turn counter is therefore an explicit implementation parity risk, not certified Houdini behavior.
entries.find_path_successor_mask_evidence: find_edge_loop and find_edge_ring pass mask 9 or 10, selecting one of QUAD_LEFT/QUAD_RIGHT together with OPPOSITE, and switch to mask 16 for boundary-only traversal when both endpoints are boundary constrained; signed left/right orientation must therefore remain explicit in the final substrate
entries.find_path_cost_substrate: group_core stores lexicographic u32 successor penalty plus f64 accumulated length and uses exact 0/1/99/100 transition costs over signed half-edge states. A deterministic circular Dial queue exploits the bounded penalty alphabet without copying Houdini heap layout. Compact CSR incidence is cached by topology pointer, P version, and query mode. Validated unblocked single-quad-disk corner queries trace both boundary chains linearly and skip unused incident sorting; all other topology and constraint classes use the complete signed-half-edge search. Licensed certification passes all ordered path cases.
entries.expand_hot_path_optimization: Expand BFS now stores its Houdini-compatible signed step result directly in one i32/-1 distance buffer instead of allocating usize distances and rematerializing i32 values; erosion negates the same buffer in place, mutually exclusive collision policies move rather than clone the collision mask, and contiguous primitive normal attributes are borrowed instead of copied.
entries.promote_output_attribute_substrate: destination group-to-integer-attribute publication and destination-group cleanup now execute inside group_core; the Group Promote node and native parity probe share the same canonical path
entries.performance_comparison_policy: requires the complete fifteen-case Houdini matrix (four single-node paths plus four-rule Range batching at 32, 128 and 256 axes), byte-exact canonical discrete input Buffer serialization, exact parameter and post-Cook group contracts, full output Geometry Cook lifecycle, and identical four-domain counts, thread count, warmups and iterations; cold, P50, P95 and isolated-process sampled Cook Working Set delta after source/parameter setup must each remain within the configured regression ratio
entries.comparison_policy: integer, topology, group membership, ordered sequence and index order are exact; every input/output additionally carries a canonical discrete-buffer JSON serialization compared byte-for-byte across providers; only floating values outside that contract use absolute plus relative epsilon; first mismatch is a JSON Pointer
entries.oracle_repeatability_policy: every Houdini and Cunning3D case performs a second untimed Cook and requires exact normalized output equality before a capture can be issued; the 77 semantic IDs are individually required exactly once

native_performance_baseline.conditions: one isolated process per node and scale; one thread; cold first cook; three warmups; fifteen measured full Geometry cooks; every measured Cook checksum asserted against the cold output outside the timed region; 1 ms single-thread Working Set sampler

repeatability.note: timings and sampled Working Set are expected to vary; both independent captures preserve the exact fifteen-case contract, parameters, per-Cook checksum assertions, and memory arithmetic gates
